name: .log
description:
View & Navigate logs as code.

Log files and console output are highlighted and navigable. Log format is detected automatically.

Read

  • Highlighting for timestamps, levels, threads, categories, IDs, and values inside messages.
  • Plain-text and JSON formats from common logging frameworks, detected per file.
  • Replace ANSI escape codes with relevant colors/styles.
  • Epoch timestamps rendered in readable date and time.
  • Growing files tailed live; large log files paginated.

Navigate

  • Ctrl+B | ⌘B on a stack frame, logger name, file path, or URL opens it.
  • Ctrl+B | `⌘B on a log message jumps to the statement that wrote it.
  • F2 / Shift+F2 cycles through errors and warnings; the Problems tool window lists them all.

Stack traces: JVM, .NET, C/C++, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby.

Consoles

  • Highlighting and links in Run, Debug, Build, Services, and Terminal output. Can be toggled off/on.
  • JSON log lines (Logback, Serilog, Pino, Winston, zerolog, …) converted to human-friendly format; right-click for the original raw JSON.

docText:
1. Open a log. Drag it into the IDE, paste the file with Ctrl+V | ⌘V, or use File | Open. *.log, *.err, *.out, *.log.txt, and *.jsonl recognized by default; add file name patterns in Settings | Editor | File Types | Logs.
  2. Jump to code. When caret is on a stack frame, a logger name, or the message text and press Ctrl+B | ⌘B.
  3. Step through problems. F2/Shift+F2 goes to the next/prev error or warning; Alt+6 / ⌘6 lists all.
  4. Console support. In Run, Debug, Build, or Terminal, the View Console as Log toolbar button switches log features for that console. JSON destructure toggle is available when JSON detected.

Live tail, ANSI, and timestamp toggles appear at the top right of the editor when detected in file content. Customize Colors/Style: Settings | Editor | Color Scheme | .log.

30-day free trial. License plans listed on the Pricing page.
